# Education in Pakistan
Pakistan's formal education system is primarily inspired by the English model and is divided into pre-school, primary, secondary, and tertiary stages. Pre-school education for ages 3–5 consists of Play Group, Nursery, and Kindergarten. Primary education (years 1–5) covers eight core disciplines including arts, general science, mathematics, and modern languages, with the language of instruction varying between English and Urdu depending on the institution. Secondary education begins in year 9 and lasts four years, culminating in the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) after year 10 and the Higher Secondary School Certificate (HSSC) after year 12. The HSSC offers various streams such as pre-medical, pre-engineering, humanities, and commerce. Alternative qualifications include the General Certificate of Education (GCE) and International Baccalaureate (IB), while technical and vocational education is offered through boards like the Punjab Board of Technical Education, providing diplomas equivalent to 12th grade.
Tertiary education in Pakistan includes professional institutes for degrees in engineering, medicine, law, and other fields, as well as universities offering bachelor's and master's degrees. Degrees are categorized as "Pass" (two years) or "Honours" (four years), with a trend toward phasing out Pass degrees. Teacher education requires 12 years of schooling followed by either an associate degree in education or a Bachelor of Education. The system faces significant challenges, including a gender disparity where female enrollment and literacy rates lag behind males, a shortage of qualified teachers, outdated curricula, and inadequate infrastructure. While the government has aimed to increase education expenditure to 7% of GDP, spending has historically remained low, hovering around 2% of GDP. Despite these issues, Pakistan has produced notable alumni in science, medicine, and economics, and international schools are becoming more prominent to cater to English-medium instruction.
